meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas (live data, not an archived version; give corpus_snapshot and source_commit). doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: GTP-loaded Rheb binds mTORC1 at the lysosome and physically re-shapes its active site into the working conformation.
data.mechanism_beginner: Switched-on Rheb docks onto mTORC1 and physically reshapes it into its working form – the actual "on" switch.
data.context: Rheb must be GTP-loaded and co-located with mTORC1. Rheb is also distributed across the ER and Golgi, and which pool supplies the activating Rheb is unresolved.
data.boundary: Cryo-EM structures, in vitro biochemistry, Drosophila and one mouse study (INOK2003, SAU2003, YAN2017, CUI2025, DEL2011) define how Rheb activates mTORC1 in reconstituted and cellular systems. Human tissue evidence is genetic and indirect: brain-restricted somatic RHEB variants in focal cortical dysplasia and hemimegalencephaly go with strong pS6 staining in the lesions (BAL2019, a cohort of 80 children in which RHEB is one of four activator genes; LEE2021, three patients). That shows the pathway running hot when Rheb is altered; it does not measure Rheb-GTP loading or mTORC1 activity directly in human tissue.
data.note: Convergence point: the amino-acid route delivers mTORC1 here, the growth-factor route delivers Rheb. Both required.

confidence.human_relevance_label: plausible in people, not shown directly
